# World — THE CONDITION REPORT

Antwerp, present day. January to May, nineteen weeks.

This world is a control system built out of paper. Nothing here is
supernatural and almost nothing here is illegal on its face. The machinery
that holds Lena Brassart in place is a filing system, a professional
register, a deed of settlement from 1974, and four people who are owed
money. Every section below exists to name a mechanism that forecloses a
choice somewhere in the outline.

---

## The Power Structure

**Corvelijn & Zonen**, Kloosterstraat 118, Antwerp. Founded 1951 by Jozef
Corvelijn, run 1988–2016 by his son Lucien, run since 2016 by Lucien's son
Sebastiaan. Six staff. The business is provenance research and restitution
brokerage: the firm finds a picture that was taken from a family between
1933 and 1945, assembles the documentary proof, represents the heirs before
the Belgian Commission for the Restitution of Cultural Property and its
foreign counterparts, and takes a contingent commission on recovery.

The commission is between twenty-two and forty per cent of hammer value,
depending on how cold the trail was. It is legal. Heirs sign for it because
without the firm they have a grandmother's anecdote and no picture. This is
the first and most important fact about Sebastiaan's power: **it is entirely
lawful and it is extractive**, and everyone involved knows both halves.

What makes his power real, in order of hardness:

1. **The claim book.** A bound register — physically bound, calfskin, updated
   by hand since 1951 and mirrored in a database — of every open claim, its
   evidentiary state, and the heirs' signed retainers. Sixty live claims
   worth, on the firm's own valuation, €38–44 million in future commission.
   The claim book is the firm's only asset of consequence. It is **firm
   property**, pledged to creditors.
2. **The index.** Forty years of Lucien's and Sebastiaan's private
   research: which picture is in which Swiss vault, which dealer's widow
   kept which ledger, which municipal archive was never digitised, which
   claims are winnable and which are bait. Eleven filing drawers and a
   laptop. The index is **Sebastiaan's personal property** under clause 14
   of the 1974 deed, because Jozef wrote it that way to keep his research out
   of his own creditors' hands. The claim book is worth money. The index is
   what makes the claim book worth money. Almost nobody in the trade
   understands that they are two different objects, and Sebastiaan has never
   corrected anyone.
3. **Reputation.** He is the man who found the Pechstein in the Ghent
   sacristy. Museums take his calls. Heirs do not shop around.
4. **Access to the docket.** A clerk at the Commission, **Bram Six**, has
   taken cash for eleven years in exchange for advance sight of filings and
   the occasional delayed date-stamp. This is the only outright corrupt
   relationship in the firm and it is worth more than everything else
   combined, because it means Sebastiaan knows what a counterparty filed
   before the counterparty's own lawyer does.

**What Sebastiaan is himself subject to.** This is the part that matters,
because a man who answers to nobody has nothing available to spend.

- **The Deurne Vier.** Four investors who bought Lucien's operating debt out
  of the 2016 estate: €4.1 million, secured by a *pledge over the claim
  book*. Chaired by **Emiel Vandewiele**, 74. They take a quarterly
  reckoning — 31 March, 30 June, 30 September, 31 December — at which
  Sebastiaan must show recoveries against forecast. Three consecutive
  misses entitles them to appoint their own administrator over the book.
  He has missed one.
- **The deed of settlement, 1974.** Jozef's instrument. It names a
  *bewindvoerder* — a steward — of the claim book, personally and
  unlimitedly liable for its administration, and binds the office to the
  eldest surviving Corvelijn while any pledge is outstanding. Sebastiaan
  cannot sell the book, cannot wind the firm up, cannot retire, and cannot
  refuse the office. **Clause 9** provides one and only one exit: a steward
  may resign by transferring the book into the escrow of a competent public
  authority, whereupon the personal liability transfers with it.
- **The Commission.** Rachida Bekkali's office can strike an intermediary
  off the register of recognised representatives. A struck intermediary
  cannot appear, cannot file, and cannot take a contingent commission in
  Belgium. The Commission cannot, however, unfile anything. Its own
  procedural rule — Article 11 — is that the docket is append-only: a
  filing can be corrected by a *corrigendum*, never withdrawn. Everything
  ever submitted stays visible forever with the correction stapled to it.
- **His own signature.** He is on the register personally, not only as a
  firm. Anything he signs, he owns.

*Iceberg:* Jozef Corvelijn's 1951 start-up capital came from somewhere and
the firm's own file on itself begins in 1953. — The pledge document has a
second schedule that Sebastiaan has never been shown, and Emiel refers to
it twice. — There is a standing instruction with the firm's bank, dated
2011, that Sebastiaan did not write and has never rescinded.

## Leverage & Exits

**What is held against Lena.**

In 1997 her father **Armand Brassart**, then the best paper conservator in
Flanders, signed a condition-and-authenticity report on a Kirchner watercolour
certifying an export licence stamp as period. The stamp was made by Lucien
Corvelijn on a Tuesday afternoon in the back room at Kloosterstraat, and
Armand watched him do it. He was paid 400,000 Belgian francs. He has never
done it again.

The report matters far past Armand. Between 1997 and 2009 Armand
authenticated the paper evidence in **twenty-two** successful restitutions.
A finding of fraud on the 1997 report is grounds for the Commission to
reopen every one of them under Article 19. Twenty-two families would face
re-litigation, and at least nine of them have already sold, which means
nine restitutions become nine debts.

Sebastiaan holds the only surviving original of the 1997 report, retrieved
from the archive of the dealer Maurice Faller when the firm bought his estate
at auction in 2019. It also implicates Lucien — but Lucien is dead, and the
dead are past prosecution, which is the whole asymmetry.

**The act itself.** On 18 January, Sebastiaan files a forty-page condition
report on the *Schindler-Wolff* Zurich claim over Lena's forged signature
and her public registration number **B-4471**. From the moment the Commission
date-stamps it, Lena is the author of record of a document she never wrote,
containing a finding she does not hold. She cannot repudiate it without
confessing to something.

**Every exit, priced.**

| Exit | What forecloses it | What trying costs |
|---|---|---|
| Resign the commission and walk | Article 11: the docket is append-only. Quitting does not unfile B-4471's report. | Nothing, and it achieves nothing. This is the trap: the door is open and the room follows her. |
| Tell the Commission the truth | Believed only if she can show who forged it, and the only proof is in his house. | Immediate suspension of B-4471 pending inquiry, minimum eleven months. Her fellowship gone. And the inquiry reaches Armand within a fortnight of opening. |
| Go to the police | Forgery of a private document requires a complainant with standing; the Schindler-Wolff heirs are the injured party, not her. The *parket* will refer it to the Commission. | Six to nine months. Same suspension. Same route to Armand. |
| Hire a lawyer | She can and does. **Advocaat Griet Vervoort**, Brussels, retainer €6,000. | She has €2,340. Vervoort works two meetings on credit and then stops. |
| The press | **Dries Neefs** ran at the firm in 2019 and was killed by the outlet's lawyers for want of documents. | He will publish only with paper. Handing him paper is itself a breach of her retainer and of the Commission's confidentiality rule — a second offence stacked on the first. |
| Leave the country | Nothing stops her. Rotterdam is ninety minutes by train. | The register is Belgian; her licence is Belgian; her father is in Berchem; the twenty-two families are here. She can leave. She cannot take any of it with her. |
| Let Armand be destroyed | Armand wants this. He says so, twice, in chapters 13 and 34. | This is the real exit, it is genuinely available from chapter 5 onward, and it costs exactly what he is worth to her. That she does not take it is a choice she makes repeatedly and must own. |

That last row is the design principle for the whole section. Lena is never
without an exit. She is without a *free* one.

**The physical constraint** arrives late and is the exception, not the rule:
15–25 March, eleven days at the Deurne depot, roller door down, no phone.
See below.

*Iceberg:* Armand kept something from 1997 that is not the report and has
never said what. — Someone paid Lena's third-year tuition in 2013 and she
has never asked her father who.

---

## Violence: Rules, Reach & Aftermath

There is very little violence in this book and every instance of it is
administrative in origin. Nobody is shot. Nobody in the trade owns a gun.
The harm here is done by keys, cold, filings and police reports.

**Who is permitted to do what.** Physical work in this world is done by
**Kasimir Ott**, 52, who runs the Deurne depot and worked for Lucien for
twenty-one years. Kasimir's own rules, which he states in chapter 10 and
believes:

1. Nothing that leaves a mark a hospital would ask about.
2. Nothing on premises the firm insures.
3. Nobody who has a lawyer on retainer.
4. Seventy-two hours, maximum, and then whatever it was has failed.

He breaks rule 4 in March, by eight days, because Sebastiaan does not
answer his phone and Kasimir has never in twenty-one years acted without an
instruction and will not start by releasing someone.

**What violence costs, physically.**

- Lena's right scaphoid was broken at nineteen, off a bicycle on the
  Kammenstraat cobbles, and united badly. It aches below about eight degrees
  and always has. Eleven days in a concrete grain store held between five
  and nine degrees, with a thermostat that runs nine minutes in fifty,
  produces a flare of that old injury plus compression numbness along the
  ulnar side of the hand from sleeping on a camp bed with a folded coat
  under the wrist. The numbness resolves in three weeks. A fine tremor,
  visible only at three times magnification, does not. For a paper
  conservator who does invisible infill under a stereo microscope, that is
  the end of one entire kind of work, permanently, and it is diagnosed in
  chapter 28 and never reversed.
- The bruising on her upper arms is finger-shaped and takes eleven days to
  yellow. She does not go to a doctor for nine days after release, which
  costs her the contemporaneous record and is the first thing Vervoort asks
  about.
- **Tomas Beke**, 36, an independent provenance researcher, is arrested on 6
  February after a stolen inventory card from the Antwerp city archive is
  found in his flat, where Kasimir put it. Charges are dropped in April for
  want of evidence. His archive accreditation is not restored, because
  accreditation is administrative and does not follow an acquittal. He is
  still selling secondhand books in chapter 36. Nobody fixes this.
- Nobody is killed in this book. **Emiel Vandewiele** dies on 8 May of a
  cardiac event in his own kitchen, at 74, having been under a cardiologist
  since November. It has nothing to do with anyone and changes a great deal.

**Who cleans up.** Kasimir, with a van and a receipt book. The depot has no
cameras — the system was specified in 2014 and never wired, and the empty
housings are still on the beams.

*Iceberg:* Kasimir keeps a ledger of favours done and owed, in a school
exercise book, and it goes back to 2003. — The depot's east bay has a
poured concrete patch, done in 2008, that is a different grey.

---

## Private Space & Access

Access in this book is asymmetric by design and the asymmetry is written
down as key-holding, not as mood.

**Kloosterstraat 118.** Four floors and a cellar, 1883, brick, on the
antiques street. Ground floor is the firm: front office, strongroom,
Sebastiaan's office with the 1974 deed framed and unread on the wall.
Smell: cold flue, hide glue, and the chip shop two doors down at six.
Keys: Sebastiaan, Kasimir, the cleaner Ineke (Tuesdays and Fridays, 6 a.m.),
and the alarm code, which is **1109** — his mother's death date, 11
September — and which he has never changed and has told nobody.

**The white room**, third floor. The conservation studio Sebastiaan built in
2017 to keep condition work in house. North light through filtered glass,
held at 50% RH and 19°C by a dehumidifier whose hum is audible everywhere
above the second landing. Smell: methyl cellulose, ethanol, and the faint
sweetness of new blotting card. The hot tap has never worked. Keys: Lena
(from 15 January), Sebastiaan. Nobody else goes up, and when the
dehumidifier stops — it cuts out when the third-floor door is held open —
that is how Lena knows someone is in the house.

**The cellar.** Sluice water audible under the floor all year. Four boxes
of Lucien's papers, unopened since 2016. Nobody has a reason to go down
there and there is no light switch at the top of the stairs.

**The Deurne depot**, Ten Eekhovelei. A 1930s grain store the firm uses for
transit and quarantine storage. Concrete floor, freight lift with a folding
gate, roller door that comes down in three stages. No heat except a wall
unit with a broken thermostat. Smell: diesel from the yard, pigeon, and the
cold mineral smell of a building that has never been warm. Keys: Kasimir,
and one spare in the firm's strongroom.

**Lena's flat**, Lange Riddersstraat, second floor rear, one room and a
kitchen, damp in the corner by the window. Hers, until 4 March, when the
building is bought by a vehicle whose sole director is a notary's clerk in
Ekeren and whose funds came from the firm's operating account. She is not
evicted. Nothing changes except that she now knows.

**The one place that is hers.** Studio 4B, the drying and pressing room at
the **Royal Academy of Fine Arts**, Mutsaardstraat. Twelve presses, a
bank of drying racks, north windows, a kettle. Access is by conservator's
key only, and there are nineteen keys. Corvelijn & Zonen has been barred
from Academy premises since a 2019 dispute over a loaned Beke study, and
the bar is a standing minute of the faculty board, which means it survives
anyone's goodwill. It is the only ground in Antwerp Sebastiaan cannot walk
onto. Lena goes there to think.

She loses the key on 27 March, when the Academy suspends her pending the
Commission inquiry. It is returned on 19 May. The fellowship it was attached
to is gone by then and does not come back.

*Iceberg:* There is a fifth box in the cellar that is not Lucien's. — The
white room's filtered glass was specified for a room facing the other way.

---

## Who Would Find Out, and What It Costs

**Rachida Bekkali**, 47, senior registrar of the Commission. She has the
power to strike the firm off the register on her own authority, and she has
suspected the firm since 2018. She is neutralized by her own institution:
striking Corvelijn & Zonen suspends sixty live claims, and sixty claims are
sixty families, several of whom are in their nineties. She will not do it on
suspicion. She has said so to Sebastiaan's face. **Concrete consequence if
she gets evidence: the firm stops trading the same afternoon.**

**Dries Neefs**, 38, investigative reporter, *De Wacht*. Ran at the firm in
2019 and had the piece killed pre-publication because everything he had was
an anonymous account of a commission rate. Neutralized by his own editor's
legal budget: he needs documents with date-stamps. **Concrete consequence if
he gets them: publication triggers the Vier's audit rights automatically
under clause 22 of the pledge**, which is exactly what happens on 12 March.

**Bram Six**, 61, Commission clerk, on the firm's money since 2013.
Neutralized by being complicit, and by a mortgage. He is the reason the 18
January filing gets a same-day date-stamp instead of sitting in a queue for
three weeks — which is the difference between Lena being able to intercept
it and not.

**Souad Ferhat**, 35, bookbinder, Lena's oldest friend. Knows almost
everything from chapter 7 onward. Not neutralized at all — she has no power
and no illusions, and what she has instead is an argument: that twenty-two
families are not Lena's arithmetic and that Lena should let Armand fall.
She is the person whose plain speech Lena cannot answer.

**Armand Brassart**, 71. Knows what he did. Wants it over. His knowledge is
the most dangerous in the book because he could end the leverage by walking
into the Commission himself, and the only thing stopping him is that his
daughter has asked him not to.

*Iceberg:* Bram Six was Lucien's contact before he was Sebastiaan's and has
never taken money from anyone else. — Rachida's own family claim was refused
in 2004 and she does not discuss it.

---

## Internal Consistency Rules

Hard constraints. Breaking one of these is a bug, not a choice.

**Reach.**
- The firm's reach is Antwerp, Brussels, the Belgian trade, and one clerk.
  It does **not** extend to: the Academy (barred by standing minute), the
  Netherlands (no relationships at all — Rotterdam is genuinely outside),
  Switzerland (the counterparty's lawyers are better resourced than the
  firm), any magistrate, or any police file once opened.
- Money in this world **can** buy: a clerk's advance copy of a docket, a
  three-day delay on a date-stamp, a locksmith, a landlord, a valuation, a
  building. Money **cannot** buy: a Commission decision, a tribunal date, an
  archive accreditation reinstated, a criminal file closed, or Ruth
  Schindler-Wolff.
- The firm is never omniscient. Sebastiaan learns things by paying Bram Six
  and by reading, and both take days. He does not know Lena went to Dries
  Neefs until it is printed. He does not know she can forge until chapter 29.

**Documents.**
- Article 11: the Commission docket is append-only. Nothing filed is ever
  removed. A corrigendum corrects; it does not erase. This rule cuts both
  ways and is the engine of the whole book.
- A corrigendum can be filed by any signatory to the original, at any time,
  without leave. This is stated on the record in chapter 7 and used in
  chapter 33. It is never a surprise.
- Article 19: a finding of fraud on any evidentiary document is grounds to
  reopen every restitution resting on that author's work.
- Registration numbers are public. Signatures are not verified at filing.
  A forgery is only caught by someone who knows the hand.

**Time and distance.**
- Antwerp–Brussels: 45 minutes by train, four an hour. Antwerp–Rotterdam:
  90 minutes. Antwerp–Basel: a flight to Zurich and a train, most of a day.
- The Commission's registry closes at 16:00 and does not accept filings out
  of hours. Twice this matters.
- Kloosterstraat to the Deurne depot: 20 minutes by van, 35 by tram and
  foot.
- The Vier's reckoning is quarterly on the last day of the quarter and
  cannot be moved.
- The Academy fellowship deadline is 1 June and is not extendable; the board
  meets once.

**Bodies.**
- A badly united scaphoid aches in cold and does not un-ache.
- Compression numbness from eleven days resolves in about three weeks; the
  microscope tremor does not resolve at all. **Nothing in the back half of
  this book gives Lena her steady hand back.**
- Bruises take eleven days to yellow and a body that was cold for eleven
  days does not sleep normally for two months.
- Emiel Vandewiele has been under a cardiologist since November. That is
  established in chapter 8 and again in chapter 16, before it is used.

**Money.**
- The firm owes €4.1m to the Vier, secured on the claim book, not on the
  index and not on the house at Kloosterstraat, which Sebastiaan owns
  personally and outright.
- The Faller matter is a Zurich tribunal proceeding in its ninth year in
  which the firm is a third-party claimant. Its timetable belongs to the
  tribunal. Nobody in this book can accelerate it, delay it, or influence
  it, and it is joked about in chapter 8 as something that will outlive
  everyone.
- Lena has €2,340 and no other family money.

**What must never happen.**
- No character acquires a capability they have not been shown to have.
- No injury heals between chapters.
- Nobody's phone conveniently lacks signal.
- The firm is never smarter in Act II than in Act III.
- No third party frees Lena. The hold is ended on 5 May by Sebastiaan
  filing a corrigendum, three days before Emiel Vandewiele dies, and that
  order is fixed.
